data.narrative:
Cerebras, a public semiconductor company founded by Andrew Feldman and four co-founders, currently trades at a $39.2B valuation after raising $6.6B+ in total funding. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 11 companies across Chips & Semiconductors: 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies including Ouster, Aeva Technologies, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, and Etched.

Peer-Median triangulation is not applicable due to an insufficient narrow peer set. Of the 10 same-sector companies identified, only 2 operate at the same stage and none at adjacent stages or within a similar valuation tier, falling short of the minimum 3-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable comparability noise given the heterogeneity of business models, customer acquisition patterns, and capex requirements within semiconductors.

Without a sufficiently dense comparable set or additional valuation methods applied to this dataset, no triangulated range can be supported. The analysis underscores a structural challenge in valuing frontier-stage semiconductor companies: the public comp set (NVDA, AMD, ALAB) operates at vastly different scales and product cycles, while private peers span technologies (quantum, lidar, AI accelerators) with limited revenue visibility. Resolving the current $39.2B valuation would require either revenue multiples against disclosed sales, DCF modeling with disclosed unit economics, or expansion of the peer set to include adjacent hardware and infrastructure sectors.
